title: Polynomial-time repetition arguments
statement: Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $s$ be a Boolean-word function and $N$ a natural-number-valued function, and suppose both $s$ and the unary word function $x\mapsto 1^{N(x)}$ are polynomial-time computable. Then the function that sends $x$ to the packed encoding of the repetition arguments—using $s(x)$ as the state word and $1^{N(x)}$ as the separate clock word—is polynomial-time computable.
replaced: If an initial-state producer and a unary-count producer are polynomial-time computable, then so is the function packing the repetition argument: the produced state word, blank call scratch, and the produced unary clock.
